title: CPI and PPI Leading Indicators Survey
tldr: Systematic review and quantitative evaluation of CPI and PPI leading indicators across short, medium, and long-term forecast horizons.
abstract: This report systematically reviews leading indicators for CPI and PPI across three forecast horizons. For CPI short-term (0-1 quarter), pork prices and oil prices are key; for core CPI medium-term (1-3 quarters), M1, social financing, long-term bond yields, PPI consumer goods sub-index, capacity utilization, fiscal spending, import price index, and unemployment rate are significant; for core CPI long-term (>3 quarters), M2, disposable income, and total factor productivity (TFP) are important. For PPI short-term, oil, nonferrous and ferrous metal prices lead; medium-term indicators include M1, PPIRM, manufacturing PMI, import prices, social financing, capacity utilization, inventory cycle, and industrial value-added; long-term factors are TFP and manufacturing FAI growth. Using univariate regression on 2012-2025 monthly data with a segmented scoring system, the study finds that for CPI, bond yields, TFP, and labor market indicators show highest elasticity, while for PPI, PPIRM and manufacturing PMI exhibit highest elasticity.
strategy: The strategy systematically identifies and evaluates leading indicators for CPI and PPI across three forecast horizons. For CPI: (1) Short-term (0-1 quarter): pork prices and international oil prices are the primary leading indicators, directly affecting CPI food and transportation components; for core CPI, services PMI business activity expectations and residential rents serve as short-term leads. (2) Medium-term (1-3 quarters): M1 growth, social financing scale, long-term bond yields, PPI consumer goods sub-index, industrial capacity utilization, government fiscal expenditure, import price index, and unemployment rate are key for core CPI. (3) Long-term (>3 quarters): M2, disposable income, and TFP are main leads for core CPI. For PPI: (1) Short-term (0-1 quarter): oil prices, nonferrous metal prices (copper, aluminum), and ferrous metal/coal prices directly drive PPI. (2) Medium-term (1-3 quarters): M1, PPIRM, manufacturing PMI, import price index, social financing, capacity utilization, inventory cycle indicators, and industrial value-added growth. (3) Long-term (>3 quarters): TFP and manufacturing fixed asset investment growth are primary indicators. Common factors (M1, M2, commodity prices, technology progress) link CPI and PPI dynamics. [source: "本文我们将梳理CPI和PPI的领先指标，并采取量化的方式评估各个领先指标的效果"]
method: The method uses univariate linear regression on monthly data from 2012 to 2025. CPI and PPI year-over-year growth rates at lag 1 month, 6 months, and 12 months serve as short-term, medium-term, and long-term prediction targets respectively. Each macroeconomic variable is regressed individually against these lagged targets to measure regression elasticity. Rather than reporting raw regression coefficients directly, a segmented scoring system is established to convert continuous statistical parameters into discrete levels, eliminating interference from dimension and volatility differences. The specific scoring rules are: coefficient absolute value in 0-0.005 scores 1 point; 0.005-0.01 scores 2; 0.01-0.1 scores 3; 0.1-0.2 scores 4; 0.2-0.5 scores 5; 0.5-1.0 scores 6; above 1.0 scores 7 points. This approach avoids underestimating the influence of high-volatility core variables whose regression coefficients may be numerically small but whose actual driving effect on CPI/PPI is substantial. [source: "我们基于2012年至2025年的月度数据，构建单变量线性回归模型进行实证检验。模型分别以滞后1个月、6个月及12个月的CPI同比增速作为短、中、长期预测目标"] [source: "系数绝对值在0至0.005区间赋1分，0.005至0.01赋2分，0.01至0.1赋3分，0.1至0.2赋4分，0.2至0.5赋5分，0.5至1.0赋6分，1.0以上赋7分"]
experiment: Using monthly data from 2012 to 2025, univariate linear regression models were constructed with lagged 1-month, 6-month, and 12-month CPI and PPI year-over-year growth rates as short-, medium-, and long-term prediction targets. The segmented scoring system (1-7 points based on coefficient magnitude) was applied to evaluate each leading indicator's regression elasticity across three time dimensions. For CPI prediction, long-term bond yields, TFP, and labor market indicators achieved the highest regression elasticity and influence scores, reflecting that financial market pricing of inflation expectations is sensitive, long-term technology supply constrains the price center, and tight labor markets drive service prices via wage transmission. For PPI prediction, PPIRM, manufacturing PMI, and production-cost indicators showed the highest elasticity, confirming PPI follows a dual logic of cost-push and demand-pull. Common factors linking CPI and PPI were identified, including M1, M2, international commodity prices, and technological progress, which serve as core connectors between consumer and producer price dynamics across different time horizons. [source: "我们基于2012年至2025年的月度数据，构建单变量线性回归模型进行实证检验"] [source: "在CPI预测中，长债收益率，全要素生产率以及就业市场指标展现出最大的回归弹性与影响力得分"] [source: "在PPI预测中，工业生产者购进价格指数、制造业PMI及相关生产端成本指标同样表现出较高的弹性"]
result: For CPI, bond yields, TFP, and labor market indicators show the highest regression elasticity. For PPI, PPIRM and manufacturing PMI exhibit the highest elasticity. The scoring system uses 7 tiers based on coefficient magnitude: 0-0.005→1pt, 0.005-0.01→2pt, 0.01-0.1→3pt, 0.1-0.2→4pt, 0.2-0.5→5pt, 0.5-1.0→6pt, >1.0→7pt. The analysis uses 2012-2025 monthly data with lags of 1, 6, and 12 months. Production materials account for about 75% of PPI. Common factors (M1, M2, commodity prices, TFP) link CPI and PPI dynamics, validating a full-cycle prediction framework.
